text.text:
Cafe Noir is perfectly located right next to Pizza 4P’s, tucked into the lively vibe of Indiranagar. We visited on a Saturday for dinner—while the indoor seating was quite full, the outdoor area was pleasantly calm (minus a few insects 🙃). The ambience overall is really inviting.

We tried their mocha frappe, which was pure bliss! Alongside that, the OG smash burger was absolutely delicious, and the prawn ravioli—wow! Easily one of the best I’ve had so far.

They also have a good selection of wine for those who enjoy it. Overall, it’s a great spot to check out if you’re in Indiranagar.

Went to Cafe Noir for lunch and it honestly exceeded expectations. Their pizzas are next level — perfectly thin crust with super fresh ingredients that you can actually taste in every bite.

We tried the burrata sun-dried tomato verde, and the cheese was chef’s kiss — so creamy and spreadable across the whole slice.

Also had the lamb ragu meatballs and prawn ravioli — both a solid 10/10.

For drinks, the crunchy Biscoff shake was so good, and ended with a blueberry croissant which is an absolute must-try ✨

I don’t drink coffee, so this review is a mix of her coffee experience and my ambience-first perspective.

Starting with the coffee (purely based on my friend’s take):
She genuinely liked it. The coffee had a strong, distinct flavour and didn’t feel like the usual “generic café coffee.” You can tell they’ve actually worked on the brew, not just served something standard.

Coming to ambience and vibe—it’s good. Not crazy, not mind-blowing, but solid Indiranagar café energy. Clean, comfortable, well-located, and easy to chill at. If you’ve been around Indiranagar cafés a lot, this won’t shock you—but it also won’t disappoint.

Food & pricing:
Everything is on the pricier side, but honestly, that’s expected for an Indiranagar café. Nothing felt bad, just not something that makes you want to come back again and again.

text.text:
Had a mixed experience at Anaia Cafe.

The pesto pasta and alfredo pasta were amazing - rich, flavourful, and perfectly cooked. The fries and garlic bread were also good.

The ambience was really nice, and service was good as well, which made the overall experience pleasant.

The only disappointment was the hot chocolate. It tasted more like Bournvita than actual hot chocolate.

The highlight of our visit was the cheesy butter garlic broccoli - so good that we ended up ordering it three times! Definitely a must-try.

Price-wise, it’s not exactly expensive, but the portions are quite small, which makes it feel a bit pricey for the quantity.

Overall, great taste and atmosphere - just wish the portion sizes were better.

text.text:
The place is spacious and looks inviting right from the outside. Once you walk in, you can choose between the upstairs and downstairs seating. We picked the upstairs section, which felt quite peaceful overall, although conversations from nearby tables were still very audible. Given the upscale pricing, I expected the tables to be spaced out a bit more.

The menu itself is quite interesting, with a lot of unique options. They also feature seasonal specials, including mango-based coffees, desserts, and baked items, and even jackfruit-inspired offerings.

Here’s what we ordered and what we thought:

Jackfruit Latte
It genuinely tastes like jackfruit because you can clearly tell they use real jackfruit purée. Unfortunately, the one we got leaned quite bitter and wasn’t particularly enjoyable for us. Maybe it would work better with added sugar, but we personally prefer our drinks without it.

Cold Coffee
This was really good. Nicely balanced and not overly sweet.

Korean Bun
Easily the highlight of our order. The bun tasted fresh, and the cream cheese filling was rich and enjoyable.

Piri Piri Fries
Pretty average overall. It didn’t really have the distinct piri piri flavour we expected.

Overall, the place has great vibes, an interesting menu, and enjoyable food.

We went to Kind on a Friday Night, it was a good place with calm vibe, we got an excellent secluded seating. The atmosphere was really great. Coming to the food, it was pretty much average. We ordered the two dimsums available in their menu, the truffle oil cream cheese dimsums was okayish, not upto the mark for me. I have had far far better ones, in Yuki, Daily Sushi and all. The other dimsum was based on thai flavours and was good, nothing awesome. Then we had ordered a Gnocchi creamy Pesto, which took them around 30 minutes to serve, don't know why. And the taste was also not upto the mark. Overall a very average experience food wise. We also ordered there walnut cake which was the best item of the day. It was really yum!!

So it's a pretty average place to be in with great vibes though. Can visit for a quick catchup with friends maybe, but definitely not for food. I have heard their coffee is good though maybe will try later someday if I like.

text.text:
Sitting right in the hustle and bustle of Indiranagar, The Kind is a one-of-a-kind comfort place for me.
The ambience wraps you up in a comforting hug with lighting that is neither scanty nor too bright. It's a place to sit with a friend, sip matcha, and catch up on things from a year ago. The waiters are the kindest, tending to your needs and wants with the best dishes.
Although I love one of the "boring" dishes: the Belgian chocolate smoothie bowl with extra almond toppings.
It's a place to sit, read, catch up, and get to know your date. Whatever may be the purpose, The Kind is the kind of answer you are looking for. It has become my regular now.

Copper + Cloves is a beautiful, plant-based oasis in Bangalore that is perfect for escaping the city's chaotic traffic. The vibe is incredibly serene, filled with lush greenery and a fantastic collection of books if you want to spend a quiet day out with clean food.

The Hits: The coconut matcha and seasonal matcha were absolutely great. The breakfast plate was amazing, and the toasties were another big hit at our table.

The Miss: The vegan khabuska was just not for us. Three of us couldn't even finish half of it, but unfortunately, we still had to pay full price for it.

Overall, it is a lovely spot for wholesome food and a peaceful atmosphere, just be mindful of what you order!

text.text:
Copper Cloves Cafe goes straight into my Top 5 worldwide. No hesitation. No debate. Just straight up there.
Their motto says “Slow Down” and somehow the whole place actually listens. The atmosphere, inside and outside, is crafted with style and soul. Books everywhere. Flowers softening every corner. Shelves that invite you to browse. A cozy kids’ space. It feels curated, not decorated.
And the food… my oh my. An unbeatable all vegan menu, sourdough that deserves its own fan club, and flavors that are thoughtful, balanced and seriously delicious. Every dish tastes like someone cared deeply before it reached your table.
The staff? 100% service minded and genuinely kind. Professional, warm, smiling. The kind of team that makes you feel welcome without hovering.
And then the magic spreads. Right there you have Love Me Twice for thrift treasures, Champaca for books you suddenly cannot live without, and No Nasties + for conscious reuse finds. The café is nestled into this whole universe like the warm heart of it all.
People stay. They read. They work. They talk. Time stretches gently. It has that Hotel California feeling, you can check out but you never really leave.
Adorable. Inspiring. Delicious. I will absolutely be back.

If you are looking for the ultimate Sunday breakfast spot, this is it. I visited with a group of friends, and it was the highlight of our weekend.

The food is absolutely fantastic. We ordered a variety of dishes to share, including a classic English breakfast and some incredible pancakes and French toast that were the perfect level of sweet. The standout for me, however, was the avocado and confit beetroot toast—the flavors were unique, fresh, and beautifully presented.

Beyond the plate, the ambience was wonderful—vibrant yet relaxed enough for a long catch-up. The service was also top-notch; the staff was attentive and friendly without being intrusive.
Highly recommended for anyone wanting a high-quality meal in a great atmosphere!

text.text:
Tried out Paper & Pie and here’s the honest take—

The vibe is clean and nice—one of those places that makes you feel slightly more productive just by sitting there.

Coffee? Solid. Egg options? Actually pretty great. Sandwiches? Let’s just say they won’t be solving world hunger anytime soon. 😄
Cold coffee was a win though, and the pudding felt like it was trying to be healthy… and mostly succeeding.

Is this some mind-blowing, life-changing café? Nah. But that’s kind of the charm.

It’s a really good spot to sit down, get some work done, have a proper conversation with a friend, or even sneak in a meeting without it feeling like a corporate box.

Overall—good food, good coffee, clean vibe, zero drama. Not extraordinary, but reliably nice… and honestly, that’s sometimes exactly what you need.
